subject: Notice: transient degradation in embedding similarity stability (us-west) — mitigation update
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@novafusion.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice: transient degradation in embedding similarity stability (us-west) — mitigation update

Hi Elaine,

I wanted to make you aware of a transient issue we detected this morning affecting embedding similarity stability for a subset of requests routed to our us-west cluster. You may see slightly different nearest-neighbor results for a small percentage of embedding queries between ~08:30–09:05 PDT. This is limited to the v1-emb-small quantized variant used by your account (we routed a portion of traffic to this flavor during a performance rollout).

What you might observe:
- Nearest-neighbor lists that change order for ~1–3% of requests
- No increase in latency or 5xx rates observed at the API layer

What we did so far:
- Scoped the impact to a config change in our quantization rollforward for the v1-emb-small profile.
- Auto-fallback to the floating-point replica for affected routing groups (this preserves result stability but increases cost per request).
- Rolled relevant routing rules back for your tenant to the pre-rollforward profile.

Attachments: kv_cache_diagnostics_0901.txt (diagnostic sample)

Immediate customer-facing mitigation: we have reactivated stable floating-point replicas for all of Novafusion's traffic and confirmed that similarity results returned to baseline for test vectors. We do not expect any data loss.

Next steps: internal RCA + a short post-incident note with recommended guardrails (we will share a link). If you want us to lock your account to FP-only for a longer window, say the word and we can configure that with no downtime.

Sorry for the disruption — we know embedding stability matters to your search syncs.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Notice: transient degradation in embedding similarity stability (us-west) — mitigation update

Thanks for the heads up — appreciate the quick rollback. A couple quick questions from our side:

1) Did any of the affected requests hit our production index during the 35-minute window? We run nightly index builds and want to know if we should re-run an integrity check.
2) Do you have a rough ETA on the RCA and the post-incident note? Our integration team will want to triage any downstream diffs.

We saw a handful of slightly reordered recommendations in the morning run (small impact, but we want to be sure).

Elaine

elaine@novafusion.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: transient degradation in embedding similarity stability (us-west) — mitigation update

Priyom / Grace — quick internal note to coordinate the customer reply.

Summary of what infra says (from the on-call trace):
- Root cause: during a staged rollforward of a quantization threshold tweak, a small subset of model shards used an older KV-caching layout. That caused deterministic differences in the embedding vectors for a small token distribution, which in turn changed cosine orderings for ~1–3% of vectors.
- Impact window: 2027-09-01T08:30:22–2027-09-01T09:05:40 PDT (us-west routing groups A1/A2).
- No 5xx errors or increased latency; only semantic variance in output.

Action taken:
- Immediate rollback of the quantization rollforward (complete 08:59 PDT).
- Forced fallback routing for customers with strict stability SLAs (Novafusion included).
- Collected KV-cache diffs and traces (attached sample).

Answers for the customer:
1) We confirmed via request replay against production indices that no writes or migrations were affected; you should not need to re-run an index build. The morning diffs you saw are consistent with the measured similarity variance and are limited in scope.
2) RCA + post-incident note ETA: we will have a customer-friendly summary by EOD 2027-09-03 and a technical RCA (internal) published to the runbook by 2027-09-06.

I recommend offering Novafusion the option to pin to FP-only for 7 days. Marcus, can you prepare the quick lock config and the cost delta?

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kv_cache_diagnostics_0901.txt]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@novafusion.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: root cause, mitigation, and next steps — Novafusion incident (Sep 1)

Hi Elaine — quick follow-up with the customer-facing summary and next steps (apologies for the slightly longer turnaround; we wanted the internal trace validated).

What happened (customer summary):
- A staged quantization tweak rolled forward to a subset of us-west shards. The change produced deterministic differences in embedding outputs for an edge token distribution used in some of your vectors. This led to small reordering in nearest-neighbor lists for ~1–3% of queries between 08:30–09:05 PDT.

What we did for you:
- Immediately rolled back the quantization change and forced your traffic onto floating-point replicas to guarantee stability.
- Confirmed via replay tests against your sample vectors that there is no data corruption; index builds are not required.
- Provided a diagnostics sample (kv_cache_diagnostics_0901.txt).

Proposed options for you:
- Keep FP-only routing for 7 days (no service interruption; cost delta will be provided by Marcus).
- Re-enable quantized profile behind a canary after we add an extra KV-cache schema compatibility check (we expect this to prevent recurrence).

Timing for docs & RCA:
- Customer-friendly incident note (public-facing summary): EOD 2027-09-03 — attached below as a link when published.
- Technical RCA and permanent guardrails: internal runbook update by 2027-09-06.

Next step from your side: let me know whether you prefer the 7-day FP-only lock or to stay on current routing and re-run a controlled canary with us. If you choose the lock, Marcus will apply it and confirm the cost delta in the next hour.

Regards,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com
